rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence (experiment 1 of 10), the priority is to establish a strong reference point for the multimodal setting, which is the natural target for 'multimodal cellular profiling.' Config_010 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt + resnet50, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) is a well-balanced, canonical multimodal configuration: scgpt provides an expressive learned RNA representation, resnet50 is a reliable pretrained image encoder, transformer aggregation captures inter-cell interactions, and concat fusion is simple and robust. Testing this first tells us (1) whether the multimodal combination is viable and at what performance level, (2) whether the chosen encoders and aggregation are adequate, and (3) gives a concrete baseline to guide ablation (e.g., swap to imagenet_vit_l, try weighted fusion, or test single-modality baselines) in subsequent experiments. It is the highest-information single experiment to anchor the remaining 9 trials.

With only one data point (config_010: multimodal, scgpt+resnet50, transformer, concat → 47.1% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion is actually contributing or whether one modality dominates. Config_001 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) is the cleanest single-modality baseline matching the RNA side of config_010 exactly. If RNA-only approaches 47%, the image modality adds little value and future effort should focus on RNA encoder/aggregation improvements. If RNA-only is substantially lower, image is critical and we should prioritize image encoder and fusion strategy experiments. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental architectural question (is multimodal worth it?) before committing remaining budget to specific improvements.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, scgpt, transformer) achieved 0.514 acc, outperforming config_010 (multimodal, scgpt, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.471 acc. The 4.3-point drop when adding the image modality via concat fusion suggests the combination strategy may be the bottleneck rather than the image features themselves. Question: Does switching from concat to weighted fusion (config_038) recover multimodal performance, isolating whether the fusion mechanism is the issue while keeping all other settings (scgpt, resnet50, transformer, multiprofile) identical to config_010? Why this is the best next step: It is a clean single-variable comparison with config_010, directly testing the most likely cause of the multimodal underperformance. If weighted fusion helps, it opens a promising multimodal direction for exploitation in remaining experiments; if it does not, it strengthens the case that resnet50 image features are uninformative here, redirecting effort toward RNA-only improvements or a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) in subsequent trials.

Evidence: RNA-only with scgpt+transformer (config_001, acc=0.514) outperforms both multimodal+resnet50 experiments (config_010 concat=0.471, config_038 weighted=0.494), suggesting ResNet50 image features are not complementing scgpt RNA features under transformer aggregation. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the image modality can add value with a different encoder, or whether the bottleneck is specifically ResNet50's feature representation. This experiment tests scgpt + imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the image encoder as the variable while keeping the best-performing RNA encoder and aggregation. If ViT also underperforms RNA-only, we gain strong evidence to pivot fully toward RNA-only optimization with the remaining 6 experiments. If it succeeds, it identifies a promising multimodal direction to exploit. This is the highest-information experiment for the central question of whether multimodal fusion can beat the current best.

The best result so far is RNA-only scgpt+transformer (0.514), while the best multimodal config is scgpt+imagenet_vit_l+transformer+concat (0.507). For the weaker resnet50 encoder, weighted fusion (0.494) outperformed concat (0.471), suggesting fusion strategy matters. Config_027 tests whether weighted fusion with the stronger ViT-L image encoder + transformer aggregation can close or close the gap to the RNA-only baseline. This is a single-variable extension (concat→weighted) of the best multimodal result, directly testing whether improved fusion can make the multimodal model competitive or superior, which is critical for exploiting the remaining 5 experiments toward the highest accuracy.

The current best is config_027 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc 0.5200). All top-performing multimodal configs used transformer aggregation, so it's unclear whether the transformer is genuinely contributing or whether the gains come solely from the image encoder and weighted fusion. Config_035 is a clean single-variable change (transformer → avgpool) from the best config, directly testing whether attention-based aggregation adds value over simpler pooling. If avgpool performs comparably, it confirms the architecture is robust and frees remaining budget to explore other dimensions (RNA encoder, profile setting). If transformer clearly wins, we've locked in the aggregation choice and can focus remaining experiments on RNA encoder or profile variations. This is the highest-information single step to reduce architectural uncertainty before committing the last 4 experiments to exploitation.

The current best (config_035, acc=0.5420) uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. Across all completed experiments, imagenet_vit_l consistently outperforms resnet50, avgpool outperforms transformer, and weighted outperforms concat. The image-side pipeline (imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) appears robust. The main untested lever is the RNA encoder: all multimodal experiments so far used scgpt, but scvi_n200 has not been paired with this winning image pipeline. Config_019 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) directly tests whether a learned generative RNA encoder can surpass scgpt while holding the strongest image-side configuration fixed. This is the highest-value experiment because it either identifies a new best configuration or confirms scgpt as optimal, reducing uncertainty on the most impactful remaining design axis with 3 experiments still in budget.

The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted (config_019) achieved 0.706, far exceeding all scgpt-based configs (~0.54 best). With only 2 experiments remaining, I want to test the most direct single-variable extension of this best config: replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping all other settings identical. Evidence from scgpt experiments (config_027 vs config_035) showed avgpool slightly outperformed transformer, but scvi_n200's richer latent representations may interact differently with transformer's token-mixing capacity. This experiment directly reduces uncertainty about whether aggregation architecture can further improve on the 0.706 result, and if it fails, confirms avgpool is optimal, allowing the final experiment to focus on a different axis (e.g., fusion type or profile setting).

Evidence: config_031 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.725) is the clear best, and all comparisons show weighted fusion outperforms concat (e.g., 0.725 vs 0.706 for transformer, 0.520 vs 0.507 for scgpt+vit). Question: config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) is the only untested variant that retains all three top-performing components (strong RNA encoder, strong image encoder, transformer aggregation) while isolating the fusion method. Why: With only 1 experiment remaining, this is the most informative test near the optimum—it confirms whether the weighted-fusion advantage persists with the much stronger scvi_n200 signal or whether concat becomes competitive, reducing residual uncertainty about the design space around the best configuration. No other untested config plausibly beats 0.725, so this is the best use of the penultimate slot.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoder pair (0.706–0.725 vs. 0.47–0.54 for alternatives), and weighted fusion as slightly superior to concat. All top-3 results use multiprofile + transformer/avgpool aggregation. However, singleprofile with the best encoders has never been tested. config_043 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) tests whether removing the multiprofile aggregation complexity (which introduces an additional modeling step) could improve generalization while retaining the proven best encoders and fusion. As the final experiment, this is the highest-value untested combination: it pairs the two clearly superior encoders with the preferred fusion strategy while exploring the one remaining architectural dimension (profile setting) that could plausibly shift performance. If it underperforms, config_031 (0.725) remains the best result.
